text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Teleworking experts who responded to an Australian Financial Review informal survey have indicated Australian business is missing out on productivity gains of 20 per cent or more as middle management refuses to allow work from home, a practice known as teleworking. Page 1.

Lend Lease Corp Ltd could become the world's biggest property funds manager, with total assets of over US$40 billion if it is able to secure the purchase of United States property group Equitable Real Estate Investment Management. Lend Lease property and investment services group manager Richard Longes said yesterday the move was the opportunity Lend Lease had been looking for. Page 1. -- According to an Australian Financial Review survey of the 63 floats in 1996, investors in share floats received a median return of 20 per cent. The survey also revealed that the best strategy for investors was to wait until after floats were listed and pick them up at a bargain price. Page 1.

After warning of a first half profit slump of as much as 50 per cent below last year, David Jones chief executive Chris Tideman said the retailer would reassess its product mix, the layout of some of its stores and its pricing policy. Tideman also said the company would consider expanding its computer and audio merchandise to offset poor sales from apparel. Page 17.

According to a report by Standard and Poor's, BHP Steel's plans to expand internationally with mini-mills in Asia could be jeopardised by a predicted large increase of steelmaking capacity around the world by the year 2000. S&P cited the assessment of the United Nations Economic Commission for Europe, which said that 76 million tonnes of new crude steel capacity would be added to the US and Asian steel industries by 1999. Page 17.

Normandy Mining Ltd is relying on its LaSource joint venture and executive Jean-Phillipe Cherrier to provide 500,000 ounces of low-cost African, Turkish and South American gold to underpin its international expansion and provide it with the credentials of a first-class global gold company. Page 18.

In its first major acquisition since the sale of two businesses last year reaped A$370 million, James Hardie Industries Ltd has bought Boral Ltd's US plasterboard operations for A$121 million. The move signals James Hardie's plans to strengthen its US plasterboard business at the same time as rapid growth in its US fibre cement operations. Page 18.

Kingstream Resources NL last week announced plans to merge with Taiwanese steel company An Feng Ltd, in a deal which will give An Feng 82.6 per cent of Kingstream and fast track the development of the A$1.4 billion MidWest steel mill in Western Australia. Page 19.
THE AUSTRALIAN

After the volatile United States Dow Jones industrial average increased more than 100 points on Friday, Australian markets are expected to rally strongly in reaction to the Wall St movement. Local economists were yesterday predicting a new record high of the all ordinaries index, which lies 25.1 away from the high set on New Year's Eve. Page 23.

WMC Ltd says it had to cancel plans to conduct a ceremony celebrating the signing of deals relating to their exciting copper discovery with three out of five of the indigenous groups who live in the region of Mt Matutum on the Filipino island of Mindanao because of demonstrations from local villagers. Page 23.

BHP Ltd has released a discussion draft that calls for a BHP Global Business Forum to be established. The Forum would be used as a guide to business conduct and ethics for the company's 65,000 employees around the world, and would offer advice on areas sch as environmental performance, occupational health and safety, workplace equality, legal compliance, the use of inside information, political contributions and financial inducements. Page 23.

Lend Lease Corp Ltd has announced it has held preliminary discussions over the purchase of Equitable Real Estate Investment Management Inc in the United States, a move that would see the company progress further into global real estate investment management. Page 25.

Barry Smorgon, of Melbourne' Smorgon family which owns PET plastics, is using his knowledge from that business to invest in a specialty plastics business in Sydney. Smorgon's purchase of a majority stake in JC Allan Australia will see him take over the position of executive chairman. Page 25.

Highlands Gold managing director Ian Goddard has said the company has given an official proposal to its Canadian suitor Placer Dome Inc which would see it selling its 25 per cent stake in Papua New Guinea's Porgera gold mine and create a new company to house its other mining assets. Page 25.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Fiery annual general meetings for the National Australia Bank and the ANZ Banking Group are expected after both banks asked shareholders to approve the issue of further share options to their chief executives. If approved, the move will see NAB chief exeutive Don Argus closing in on Westpac managing director Robert Joss as Australia's best paid banker. Page 11.

Property and finance giant Lend Lease said yesterday it was negotiating to purchase the Equitable Real Estate Investment Management (ERE), the largest United States manager of real estate and mortgage investments. While not disclosing a purchase price, Lend Lease could be expected to pay at least A$300 million for the group if the negotiations succeed. Page 11.

Canadian group Placer Dome, a 44 per cent shareholder in Highlands Gold, is expected to respond this week to Highlands' proposal yesterday of a A$185 million capital return to all shareholders other than Placer Dome and the spin-off of a new group that would own its non-Porgera assets. The deal would see Placer Dome getting Highlands' 25 per cent interest in Porgera. Page 12.

The Musgrave Block in the north-west of South Australia could replace the Gawler Craton in the State's centre as the next big region of exploration in 1997. The area has been seized on by large miners, including RTZ-CRA, Delta Gold DEL.AX and Goldsearch. Page 1.

As gold stocks come under pressure today following the drop in the price of gold to US$360.80 an ounce, Porter Western chartist Shane Gherbaz said he expected the price of gold to fall further before bottoming out and starting a recovery, and Crosesus Minng chairman Ron Manners, from the gold heartland of Kalgoorlie, acknowledged the weekend fall was "a pretty serious drop". Page 12.

Neil Cribb, senior manager of Bird Cameron's Perth reconstruction and insolvency division, has warned people who amend their wills to ensure none of the beneficiaries will face the threat of bankruptcy. Cribb said bankruptcy laws say that any property or assets acquired by a bankrupt had to be made available to that person's creditors, and this includes any proceeds from a deceased estate. Page 13.
THE AGE

According to The Age's six-monthly survey of 28 economists from business, academia and the financial sector, growth will continue to fall in 1997 and there will be little improvement in unemployment. Half of those surveyed thought the Reserve Bank should cut interest rates early in the new year. Page C1.

Despite hints last month of a National Australia Bank court challenge to the A$2.65 billion proposed merger between Advance Bank and St George Bank, a source close to Advance does not expect NAB to make submissions against the Supreme Court's approving the scheme when the banks' make their application today. Page C1.

Following a strong rebound on Wall Street at the weekend, the Australian sharemarket is set for a strong opening, with the Dow Jones surging 101.59 points or 1.58 per cent to 6544 points. However, the weakness in the gold sector will continue after a slie of US$4.60 an ounce in the New York gold price to US$362. Page C1.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
